historical_record.description: The first building on the lot was put up in 1869 by A. J. Downer, a commission merchant.
By the mid-1880s the lot held a square two-story house with a flat front, then numbered 1104 Taylor Street, possibly the 1869 building.
Around 1900 a two-story building of two flats, with two bay windows on the street, replaced the earlier house; William Keating owned the lot by then.
The 1906 earthquake and fire burned through residential Nob Hill and destroyed the two-flat building on this lot; only elements of pre-1906 foundations survive in the present basement.
The present one-story Neo-Georgian cottage was built in 1906 for William Keating, a coachman to the Flood family, to plans by Stone & Smith that were ready five months after the earthquake.
The original metal-shingle roof was replaced with asbestos shingles.
Several years after William Keating's death his widow transferred the house to a family relation, keeping it in the Keating family.
The Keating family's ownership ended when the house was sold in 1936.
The house was sold in 1976 to the owners who held it when it was designated.
The window panes on the Taylor Street front were replaced.
After a break-in, scroll-pattern metal security grilles were fitted over the windows and a metal gate was put up at the south end of the street front.
A stained-glass panel was set into a street-front window and the house was re-roofed, following a stained-glass entry transom added in 2003.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 251, Glazer-Keating House.

notable_residents.name: William Keating
notable_residents.detail: William Keating, an Irish-born coachman long employed by the Flood family, built and owned the cottage and lived here until his death.
